ticket_types.label: ACL – Permit / Allow Traffic
ticket_types.concept:
Traffic is being dropped by the firewall because no explicit permit rule exists for the requested flow, or a deny rule is evaluated before the permit. Cisco ASA/Firepower processes ACLs top-down and is stateless for ACL evaluation — bi-directional traffic requires explicit permit entries on both the source-side interface ACL and the destination-side interface ACL.

Root causes:
  1. No permit rule exists for the source/destination pair
  2. An east-west deny rule (e.g. object-group FW-SEGMENTS) blocks the traffic
  3. Routing is missing — firewall has no route to the destination subnet
  4. Wrong interface ACL is being checked

Approach: Identify interfaces → verify routing → simulate with packet-tracer → identify drop reason → insert permit rules ABOVE deny entries on both ACLs → validate → test from host.
precheck: ! --- Identify which interfaces own the source and destination subnets ---
! --- Verify routing exists for source and destination ---
! --- Check which ACL is applied inbound on each relevant interface ---
! --- Review the full ACL for existing rules and hit counts ---
! --- Check for object-groups that may block east-west traffic ---
prep: ! PREP — Add permit rules (BOTH directions required)
! --- Permit SOURCE to DESTINATION (on source-side interface ACL) ---
access-list <ACL_NAME> line 5 extended permit <PROTOCOL> host <SOURCE_IP> host <DEST_IP>
access-list <ACL_NAME> line 5 extended permit tcp host <SOURCE_IP> host <DEST_IP> eq <PORT>
! --- Permit DESTINATION to SOURCE return traffic (on destination-side ACL) ---
access-list <DST_ACL_NAME> line 5 extended permit <PROTOCOL> host <DEST_IP> host <SOURCE_IP>
! --- Verify hit count on new permit rules ---
rollback: ! ROLLBACK — Remove the permit rules added in PREP
no access-list <ACL_NAME> extended permit <PROTOCOL> host <SOURCE_IP> host <DEST_IP>
no access-list <ACL_NAME> extended permit tcp host <SOURCE_IP> host <DEST_IP> eq <PORT>
no access-list <DST_ACL_NAME> extended permit <PROTOCOL> host <DEST_IP> host <SOURCE_IP>

check.confirm: Customer requires bi-directional network connectivity between <SOURCE_IP> and <DEST_IP> on port <PORT>/<PROTOCOL>. This is a firewall ACL change to allow the specified traffic flow. No security risk has been identified as the hosts are owned by the customer.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm Account Admin or authorised requester has approved this change.
! Record the name and permission level of the approver.
check.ensure:
! Confirm you are working on the correct device:
show version | in Hostname
show version | in Device
! Cross-reference device ID from ticket with CMDB/nscli output

comprehend.what_could_break: If inserted at wrong line number, permit rule may not be evaluated before the deny. Other hosts not in the rule will be unaffected.
comprehend.expected_result: Traffic between <SOURCE_IP> and <DEST_IP> on <PORT> will be permitted in both directions.
comprehend.other_teams: NA — firewall change only. No routing or application team impact.

know_change: access-list <ACL_NAME> line 5 extended permit <PROTOCOL> host <SOURCE_IP> host <DEST_IP>
access-list <DST_ACL_NAME> line 5 extended permit <PROTOCOL> host <DEST_IP> host <SOURCE_IP>

ticket_types.label: ACL – Deny / Block IP Address
ticket_types.concept:
Malicious or unwanted traffic must be blocked by inserting deny rules at a line number ABOVE any broad permit entries. Cisco ASA/Firepower evaluates ACLs top-down — if a wide permit rule appears before the deny, the deny is never reached (hit count = 0 confirms this).

Two-phase approach:
  Phase 1 — Immediate containment: shun <IP> drops active sessions instantly (not persistent across reload).
  Phase 2 — Permanent block: Add IP to BLACKLIST_IPs object-group and reference it in an ACL deny rule positioned above the broad permit.

Using object-groups is best practice — allows future IPs to be added without touching the ACL itself. FQDN-based sources require an 'object network' entry with 'fqdn' keyword before being added to the group.
precheck: ! --- Check if IP is already blocked (avoid duplicates) ---
! --- Check existing ACL deny entries for this IP ---
! If hit count = 0, the deny rule exists but is never reached (rule order issue)
! --- Identify the broad permit rule that traffic is currently matching ---
! Look for the rule with the highest hit count
! --- Simulate current traffic path (confirm currently ALLOWED) ---
! Expected BEFORE fix: Action: allow (this confirms the problem)
prep: ! Note: shun is NOT persistent across reload
! --- PHASE 2: Remove existing ineffective deny rules (if hit count = 0) ---
no access-list <ACL_NAME> extended deny ip host <SOURCE_IP> any
no access-list <ACL_NAME> extended deny tcp host <SOURCE_IP> host <DEST_IP> eq <PORT>
! --- PHASE 4: Insert deny rule ABOVE the broad permit (line 19 typical) ---
access-list <ACL_NAME> line 19 extended deny ip object-group BLACKLIST_IPs any
! --- PHASE 5: Remove temporary shun (permanent ACL rule now active) ---
rollback: ! ROLLBACK — Remove block (if applied in error)
no access-list <ACL_NAME> extended deny ip object-group BLACKLIST_IPs any

check.confirm: Customer requests permanent block of <SOURCE_IP> which has been identified performing <ATTACK_TYPE> attacks against <DEST_IP>. Request pre-approved by <APPROVER_NAME>.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm Account Admin or authorised requester has approved this block.
! Auto-approved by <APPROVER_NAME> per ticket notes.
check.ensure:
show version | in Hostname
! Confirm correct firewall device — cross-reference ticket device IDs.

comprehend.what_could_break: If the IP belongs to a legitimate user, blocking it will cause service interruption. Pre-check confirms it is malicious.
comprehend.expected_result: Traffic from <SOURCE_IP> will be permanently dropped. No active sessions will be maintained from this IP.
comprehend.other_teams: NA — security block only. SOC/security team notified via ticket.

know_before: ! Expected BEFORE: IP not present in any block group
know_change: access-list <ACL_NAME> line 19 extended deny ip object-group BLACKLIST_IPs any
know_after: ! Expected AFTER: IP present in BLACKLIST_IPs

ticket_types.label: Object-Group – Create / Modify
ticket_types.concept:
When a new network site or subnet needs to be included in existing firewall policy, the cleanest approach is creating a new named object-group for that site's subnet and nesting it into the existing parent aggregate group using 'group-object'. This avoids modifying access-lists directly — all rules referencing the parent group automatically extend to the new subnet.

Pre-checks verify the subnet is not already present (to avoid duplicates) and confirm the parent group exists. The blast radius is limited to traffic from/to the new subnet only.
precheck: ! --- Confirm the subnet does NOT already exist in config ---
! --- Check what ACLs reference the parent group (understand blast radius) ---
! --- Confirm new sub-group does NOT already exist ---
prep: ! PREP — Create new object-group and nest into parent
! --- Create new object-group for the new site ---
! --- Nest new group into parent aggregate group ---
rollback: ! ROLLBACK — Remove object-group and unlink from parent
! --- Delete the sub-group (only if not referenced elsewhere) ---

check.confirm: Customer requests creation of a new object-group <NEW_GROUP_NAME> for site <SITE_NAME> with subnet <SUBNET>/<MASK>, to be nested into the existing <PARENT_GROUP> aggregate group so that firewall policies automatically apply to the new site.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm authorised requester has approved this network policy change.
check.ensure:
show version | in Hostname
! Confirm device. Verify <PARENT_GROUP> exists with: show run object-group id <PARENT_GROUP>

comprehend.what_could_break: If <PARENT_GROUP> is referenced in a deny rule, the new subnet will also be denied. Confirm the parent group intent before nesting.
comprehend.expected_result: All existing firewall rules referencing <PARENT_GROUP> will automatically apply to <SUBNET>. No direct ACL modification required.
comprehend.other_teams: NA — firewall object change only. No routing changes required if subnet is directly connected.

ticket_types.label: NAT – Translation / DNS Rewrite Issue
ticket_types.concept:
NAT issues typically present as DNS resolving to wrong IP (external instead of internal SNAT IP for inbound traffic), or traffic failing to translate. On Cisco ASA, manual NAT takes precedence over auto NAT. Missing 'dns' keyword in static NAT causes DNS responses to not be rewritten. Compare a working NAT rule against the broken one — the difference reveals the root cause.

For Cisco ASA: 'nat (inside,outside) source static ... dns' enables DNS doctoring.
Verify using 'show xlate' for active translations and 'show nat detail' for hit counts.
precheck: ! --- Check existing translations for affected IP ---
! --- Compare working vs broken NAT rule ---
prep: ! --- Option A: Add DNS keyword to existing static NAT ---
no nat (<INSIDE_IF>,<OUTSIDE_IF>) source static <LOCAL_OBJ> <GLOBAL_OBJ> destination static <REMOTE_OBJ> <REMOTE_OBJ>
nat (<INSIDE_IF>,<OUTSIDE_IF>) source static <LOCAL_OBJ> <GLOBAL_OBJ> destination static <REMOTE_OBJ> <REMOTE_OBJ> no-proxy-arp route-lookup dns
! --- Option B: Create new object NAT ---
rollback: no nat (<INSIDE_IF>,<OUTSIDE_IF>) source static <LOCAL_OBJ> <GLOBAL_OBJ> destination static <REMOTE_OBJ> <REMOTE_OBJ> no-proxy-arp route-lookup dns
! --- Restore original NAT rule (without dns keyword) ---
nat (<INSIDE_IF>,<OUTSIDE_IF>) source static <LOCAL_OBJ> <GLOBAL_OBJ> destination static <REMOTE_OBJ> <REMOTE_OBJ> no-proxy-arp route-lookup

check.confirm: Customer reports DNS resolving <FQDN> to incorrect IP when queried from internal hosts. Expected internal resolution is <INTERNAL_IP>. Root cause identified as missing DNS rewrite in NAT configuration.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm authorised requester has approved this NAT change.
check.ensure:
show version | in Hostname
show run nat | in <DEST_IP>

comprehend.what_could_break: Existing sessions using old translation may reset. DNS cache on internal servers may need clearing after change.
comprehend.expected_result: Internal servers will resolve <FQDN> to <INTERNAL_IP>. Traffic will route internally via SNAT rather than hairpinning via external IP.
comprehend.other_teams: Application team may need to clear DNS cache post-change.

know_change: nat (<INSIDE_IF>,<OUTSIDE_IF>) source static <LOCAL_OBJ> <GLOBAL_OBJ> destination static <REMOTE_OBJ> <REMOTE_OBJ> no-proxy-arp route-lookup dns
know_after: ! Expected: translation present with DNS rewrite

ticket_types.label: VPN – Site-to-Site Tunnel (IKEv1/IKEv2)
ticket_types.concept:
Site-to-site VPN failures fall into three categories:
  Phase 1 (IKE): mismatched proposals, PSK, or peer unreachable
  Phase 2 (IPsec): mismatched transform-set or proxy IDs
  Traffic not interesting: crypto ACL mismatch

Diagnostic sequence:
  1. Check show crypto isakmp sa for Phase 1 state (should be MM_ACTIVE/QM_IDLE)
  2. Check show crypto ipsec sa for encaps/decaps counters incrementing
  3. Run packet-tracer to confirm traffic hits crypto map
  4. Bounce tunnel with vpn-sessiondb logoff to force renegotiation

Both sides must have identical IKE proposals, transform-sets, PSK, and mirror-image crypto ACLs.
precheck: ! --- Check Phase 2 IPsec SA state and counters ---
! Check encaps and decaps counters — should increment
! --- Verify route to peer IP exists ---
! --- Simulate traffic to confirm crypto is hit ---
prep: ! PREP — VPN Tunnel Fix (choose applicable option)
! --- OPTION A: Bounce VPN session (stuck negotiation) ---
! --- OPTION B: Fix IKEv1 Phase 1 policy mismatch ---
crypto ipsec ikev1 transform-set TS esp-aes esp-sha-hmac
! --- OPTION E: Fix crypto ACL (add missing network) ---
rollback: no access-list VPN-ACL extended permit ip <LOCAL_NET> <LOCAL_MASK> <REMOTE_NET> <REMOTE_MASK>

check.confirm: Customer reports VPN tunnel to peer <PEER_IP> is down. Traffic from <SOURCE_IP> to <DEST_IP> is failing. Tunnel requires re-establishment. <DESCRIPTION_OF_CHANGE>.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm authorised requester has approved this VPN change.
check.ensure:
show version | in Hostname
show crypto isakmp sa | in <PEER_IP>

comprehend.what_could_break: All traffic traversing this VPN tunnel will be interrupted during renegotiation (typically 2-5 seconds for bounce). PSK changes affect both sides — coordinate with remote peer team.
comprehend.expected_result: VPN tunnel to <PEER_IP> will be established. show crypto isakmp sa will show QM_IDLE/MM_ACTIVE. encaps/decaps counters will increment.
comprehend.other_teams: Remote site team must be notified for PSK or proposal changes — both sides must match.

know_before: ! Note current SA state and counters

ticket_types.label: VPN User – Create / Modify
ticket_types.concept: VPN user creation on Cisco Firepower requires manual execution when automation fails (HA detection error, partial automation failure). The 'username' command in global config creates local VPN users. Always verify the user does not exist first. The user's attributes (group policy, VPN filter) can be assigned post-creation. Credentials must be shared securely via approved channel.
precheck: ! --- Check current group-policy for VPN users ---
prep: ! Expected: username entry present with correct attributes
rollback: ! Expected: no output (user does not exist)

check.confirm: Customer requests creation of VPN user <USERNAME> on device <DEVICE_ID>. This is a customer-owned VPN with an existing group-policy. Automation failed due to <AUTOMATION_ERROR>.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm Account Admin has approved this user creation.
check.ensure:
show version | in Hostname
! Confirm working on correct firewall device.

comprehend.what_could_break: If a duplicate username exists, the password will be overwritten. Pre-check confirms user does not exist.
comprehend.expected_result: New VPN user <USERNAME> created. Customer can authenticate via VPN using provided credentials.
comprehend.other_teams: NA — credentials to be shared with customer via secure channel.

know_before: ! Expected BEFORE: no output (user does not exist)
know_after: ! Expected AFTER: username <USERNAME> present in config

ticket_types.label: Firewall – Software Upgrade (Maintenance)
ticket_types.concept:
Firewall software upgrades are planned maintenance events requiring:
  1. Full pre-change baseline (version, VPN state, routing, ping sweep)
  2. Config backup locally and to TORQ
  3. Rollback boot variable set to CURRENT image BEFORE setting new image
  4. New image boot variable set
  5. Reload and post-validation

The rollback boot variable is critical — if post-upgrade validation fails, a simple reload returns to the previous known-good image without any config work. Never upgrade without a confirmed rollback path.
precheck: ! --- Verify new image is present on disk ---
! --- VPN tunnel baseline (record all active tunnels) ---
prep: ! --- STEP 1: Set rollback boot variable (CURRENT image) ---
! This is mandatory BEFORE setting new image
! Confirm CURRENT image is set as boot system
! --- STEP 2: Set new image as boot target ---
! POST-RELOAD VALIDATION (connect after device comes back up)
rollback: ! ROLLBACK — Boot back to previous image

check.confirm: Planned maintenance to upgrade firewall software on device <DEVICE_ID> from version <CURRENT_VERSION> to <TARGET_VERSION>. Change window: <MAINTENANCE_WINDOW>.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
nscli zsp unlock <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm authorised change approver. Alert suppressions added.
check.ensure:
show version | in Hostname
show disk0: | in <NEW_IMAGE>
! Confirm new image is present on device storage.

comprehend.what_could_break: Reload causes approximately 3-5 minutes of downtime. All VPN tunnels will drop and renegotiate. If new image has issues, rollback boot variable allows recovery on next reload.
comprehend.expected_result: Device will reload and boot on <TARGET_VERSION>. All VPN tunnels will re-establish. Network reachability will match pre-upgrade baseline.
comprehend.other_teams: NOC team must be notified. Alert suppressions required during maintenance window.

know_after: ! Expected: all previously reachable IPs still reachable

ticket_types.label: Interface – Down / Error / Duplex
ticket_types.concept: Interface issues are caused by physical problems (cable, SFP, remote device failure), configuration mismatches (duplex/speed auto-negotiation failure), or administrative shutdown. CRC errors indicate physical layer issues or duplex mismatch. Flapping suggests SFP/cable instability or STP topology changes. The diagnostic sequence is: physical check → show interfaces for counters → check running-config for shutdown/speed/duplex → check CDP for remote device state.
precheck: ! --- Check running config for this interface ---
! --- Check CDP for remote device state ---
prep: ! --- OPTION A: Bring up admin-shutdown interface ---

check.confirm: Interface <INTERFACE> on device <DEVICE_ID> is reported down/degraded. Customer reports <SERVICE_IMPACT>. Root cause to be identified and resolved.
check.have:
nscli permissions t <TICKET_ID>
! Confirm authorised change approval.
check.ensure:
show version | in Hostname
show interfaces <INTERFACE>

comprehend.what_could_break: Flapping interface may affect STP topology. Bringing up a previously shutdown port may introduce unexpected traffic. Verify with customer before enabling.
comprehend.expected_result: Interface <INTERFACE> will be in up/up state with no error counters incrementing.
comprehend.other_teams: If interface carries customer-facing traffic, notify customer before and after change.

know_before: ! Note current state and error counts
know_after: ! Expected: <INTERFACE> is up, line protocol is up
